verdict.rationale: GitHub's own docs describe fine-grained personal access tokens. When you create one, you grant it a specific set of permissions that define which resources it can reach through the API. The `X-Accepted-GitHub-Permissions` response header tells you exactly which permissions an endpoint needs, so you can give an agent only what it requires. missing for 10: evidence of per-repository scoping and token expiration controls, an agent- or app-specific credential type distinct from personal tokens, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
